questions.q: What is Power BI's usage metrics report?
options: A manually maintained spreadsheet that owners fill in by hand
An auto-generated Power BI report, built once usage metrics is turned on, showing views, viewers, and views-by-user
A setting that automatically deletes unused reports
A certification requirement every dataset must pass before publishing
questions.explain: Turning usage metrics on generates a real, automatically built Power BI report covering views, viewers, and a views-by-user breakdown.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call the 'Views by user' table the most important piece for governance?
options: Because it's the only chart that uses color
Because it ties usage to specific, named people rather than just a total count
Because it shows the report's DAX formulas
Because it's required for certification
questions.explain: Views by user turns 'people use this' from an assumption into a specific, named list — which matters directly when deciding who to notify about a change.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a certified dataset with zero recent views suggest to a governance reviewer?
options: Nothing — certified datasets never need to be reviewed again
That the data source is definitely corrupted
A red flag: either the dataset is genuinely obsolete, or people have quietly moved to an uncertified substitute
That the dataset should immediately be deleted with no further review
questions.explain: Zero views on certified content is a signal worth investigating — it may mean the certification is stale, or worse, that people have drifted to an unreviewed alternative.

questions.q: Where is 'View usage metrics report' located in the Power BI service?
options: Only accessible through PowerShell
In the same '...' / More options menu as other item actions, alongside things like View workspace lineage
It must be requested from Microsoft support
Inside Power BI Desktop only, never in the service
questions.explain: It sits in the standard item menu right alongside other per-item actions like viewing lineage — not off in a separate admin-only location.

questions.q: What does the Fabric monitoring hub add that one report's usage metrics doesn't cover?
options: It shows the exact DAX code behind every measure
A tenant-wide view of job runs — refreshes, dataflow runs, deployment pipeline jobs — across every item an admin can see
It replaces the need for endorsement entirely
It's identical to usage metrics, just renamed
questions.explain: Usage metrics covers one report's views. The monitoring hub is a tenant-wide operational view of job runs, catching things like failed refreshes before users notice stale data.
